title: Confirm intent-1: EC#13 is the odd one out of the 8 output couplers (y=-187.5, pitch 124/130 instead of 127)
evidence: Twin group = 8 output edge couplers (all the same PDK cell, fingerprint edca35fe1ccc, equal to a fresh lx.edge_coupler()). rv.instances() y: 444.5, 317.5, 190.5, 63.5, -63.5, -187.5, -317.5, -444.5 -> 7 on the 127 um grid, EC#13 3.0 um high. Mirror XOR of the whole chip about y=0 (work/twins/s6.py): SLAB_NEGATIVE differs only at the EC#10/EC#13 windows (two 360x3 um strips each side). route_out_5 s-bend normalised against route_out_0: Hausdorff 3.0 um, dy 58.85 instead of 61.85 (still R=80: tan(t/2)=58.85/123.97 -> R=80.0). Path to EC#13 is 1.45 um shorter than the reference path (2011.47 vs 2012.92 um of routes).
impact: Fibre array (127 um) aligned to the other 7: 3 um offset on a ~3 um MFD -> ~17 dB, channel lost. LVS connects it, so only a pitch check sees it.
fix: Place EC#13 at (2700, -190.5) and route route_out_5 with the same 61.85 um R=80 s-bend as its twins.

title: Confirm intent-2: route_l1_1 vertical straight 0.30 um off the axis of its own bends; its mirror twin route_l1_0 is on axis
evidence: Twin pair route_l1_0 / route_l1_1 (mirror about y=0). Mirror XOR of LN_RIDGE: 92.35 um x 0.6 um strip at x 656.95..657.55 and 0.3 um strips at x 656.25..656.55, y +-81.65..+-174.0. rv.cross_section(657,-120,90): ridge centre x=657.05; rv.cross_section(657,100,90) (twin): x=656.75. Slab of the same straight is NOT shifted (centre 656.75 in both). Bends are identical to the twin (R=80, 125.66 um, XOR < 0.04 um2). rv.junction_loss(1.0,1.0,offset=0.3) = 0.903 dB per step (I re-ran it), two steps.
impact: About 1.8 dB on outputs EC#12..EC#15 (half the tree); uneven 1x8 split. Exceeds the 1 dB critical limit.
fix: Put the straight on x=656.75 (centre of the bend ends), as in route_l1_0.

title: Confirm intent-3: route_l2_2 is the only level-2 route with a 10 um ridge gap (ridge drawn on LN_SLAB)
evidence: Twin group = 4 level-2 routes; after normalising (translate to start pin, mirror) the s-bends are identical (XOR <= 0.024 um2, Hausdorff <= 6 nm). route_l2_2 vs its mirror twin route_l2_1: LN_RIDGE XOR = exactly 10.0 um2 at x 1546.846..1556.846, y -127.5..-126.5, and route_l2_2 carries a 10x1 um LN_SLAB patch there (cell_shapes: 3 LN_SLAB shapes vs 2 in the twins). rv.lvs(): design_only [MMI#3.P2, MMI#6.P0].
impact: 10 um with no lateral guide plus two ridge/slab steps: several dB on EC#12 and EC#13 (agree with intent-3 estimate).
fix: Draw the 10 um piece on LN_RIDGE (remove the LN_SLAB patch).

title: Confirm intent-4: 0.5 um LN_RIDGE gap in route_in at x 489.239..489.739 (no twin; rv.drc() and rv.lvs() flag it)
evidence: rv.cell_shapes("route_in"): ridge 360.0..489.239 and 489.739..500.0, slab continuous 360..500 (10 um). rv.drc(): LN_RIDGE.space<1.0 marker [489.239,-1,489.739,1]. rv.lvs() design_only [EC#0.P0, MMI#1.P0]. All other pin-to-pin junctions on the chip are continuous (cross-sections at +-0.02 and +-0.3 um of every pin, work/twins/s9.py).
impact: Common input: every output loses the same amount (estimate 0.1 to 0.5 dB, see intent-4); above the 0.05 dB limit.

title: Confirm intent-5 with a higher loss: route_out_6 (two R=25 um 90-deg bends) is the only output route not built from s-bends; ~0.9 dB, not 0.3-0.6
evidence: Twin pair route_out_1 / route_out_6 (both 61.85 um offset); 5 other output routes are R=80 s-bends identical within 6 nm. route_out_6 ridge: 2 x 39.268 um (= pi/2 x 25.0) + 11.85 + 513.25 um. rv.modes(1.0, bend_radius=25): TE0 38.4 dB/cm (R=80: 0.02 dB/cm) -> 0.30 dB radiation over 78.5 um. Straight-to-bend TE0 mode overlap (rv._solve straight vs bend, same overlap formula as rv.junction_loss; work/twins/s5.py): R=25 0.178 dB, R=80 0.013 dB (solver/grid floor) -> ~0.165 dB per transition x 4 transitions = ~0.66 dB. Path to EC#14: 2034.00 um of routes vs 2012.92 um reference (+21.08 um).
impact: Estimated 0.6 to 1.0 dB extra on EC#14 (on top of the 1.8 dB of intent-2 and 0.06 dB of intent-6 on the same path, so EC#14 is ~2.8 dB below the upper channels); +21 um length (42x the tolerance).
fix: Replace with the same 61.85 um R=80 s-bend as route_out_0/7 (dx 126.36 um).

title: Confirm intent-6: route_l2_3 straight is 0.6 um wide; its 3 level-2 twins are 1.0 um
evidence: Twin group of 4 level-2 routes: mirror XOR shows two 367.046 x 0.2 um strips along y=-381.5..-381.3 and -380.7..-380.5; s-bends equal. Pin check at MMI#7.P0 (1700,-381): ridge 0.6 um at x-0.02, 1.0 um at x+0.02. My rv.modes(0.6): n_eff 1.7416, n_g 2.1505 vs 1.7915 / 2.1898; rv.junction_loss(1.0,0.6) = 0.030 dB per step.
impact: ~0.06 dB on EC#14/EC#15 and a group-delay skew equal to ~6.6 um of route (13x the +-0.5 um tolerance).

title: Confirm intent-7: 0.4 um x 2 um neck in route_l1_0; its mirror twin route_l1_1 has none
evidence: Mirror XOR of l1 pair, vertical straight: ridge XOR 55.38 um2 includes the 0.4 um piece at x 656.55..656.95, y 136.718..138.718 (6 ridge shapes vs 4 in the twin). rv.cross_section(656.75,137.7,90) = 0.4 um. rv.junction_loss(1.0,0.4) = 0.167 dB per step (re-run).
impact: Up to ~0.33 dB on EC#8..EC#11 (the 2 um length is short, so the real value may be lower; still above 0.05 dB).

title: Confirm intent-8: route_out_1 s-bend R=100 (dx 144.62 um) vs R=80 (dx 126.36 um) in its 5 s-bend twins; -2.27 um path
evidence: Two-arc s-bend fit: tan(t/2) = 61.85/144.619 -> t = 46.3 deg, R = 144.619/(2 sin t) = 100.0 um, arc length 161.65 um (measured 161.65 from perimeter). Twins: 61.85/126.359 -> R = 80.0, 145.66 um. Route sums (centre line from perimeter, work/twins/s3.py): path EC#9 2010.65 um vs 2012.92 um reference.
impact: No extra loss; length intent broken by 2.27 um (4.5x tolerance).
fix: Use the R=80 s-bend of the twins.

title: Confirm intent-9 (harmless): MMI#5 is 0.3 um right of its 3 stage-3 twins, but its routes absorb it exactly
evidence: Stage-3 MMI x: 1725.0, 1725.3, 1725.0, 1725.0 (rv.instances()). route_l2_1 straight 367.346 (+0.300), route_out_2/3 straights 436.591 (-0.300); s-bends identical to twins (XOR 0). Pins P0/P1/P2 of MMI#5 continuous and on axis (work/twins/s9.py). Path lengths EC#10/EC#11 = 2012.919 um = reference.
fix: Optional: move back to 1725.0 for a clean table.

title: Confirm intent-10 (harmless): route_out_0 straight 10 nm off axis
evidence: route_out_0 vs twin route_out_7 (mirrored): straight XOR = two 436.891 x 0.01 um strips, Hausdorff 0.01 um; EC#8 pin cross-section: ridge centre +0.01 before x=2340, 0.0 after. rv.junction_loss(1.0,1.0,offset=0.01) = 0.001 dB (re-run).

title: Loss check for intent-3/rules-2: eigenmode expansion gives ~5.4 dB for the 10 um slab-only section of route_l2_2
evidence: work/twins/s11.py: local mode solves on a 14 um plane, ridge TE0 (RWG1000, n_eff 1.7915) projected onto 40 modes of the slab-only section (route LN_SLAB 10 um, ridge drawn on LN_SLAB; n_eff 1.657..1.381), propagated and projected back. 40 modes hold 91.8 % of the power (basis floor 0.74 dB at L=0). T(L): 0.5 um 0.78 dB, 1 um 0.90, 2 um 1.36, 5 um 3.28, 10 um 5.41 dB. Agrees with rules-2 (~6 dB) and intent-3 (5-7 dB). For the 0.5 um gap of intent-4 the same model only bounds the loss (0.04 dB excess over the basis floor to 0.78 dB upper bound), consistent with rules-1 (0.3-0.7 dB).
impact: EC#12 and EC#13 about 5 to 6 dB down (EC#13 is also dead at the fibre array, intent-1).
fix: Draw the 10 um piece on LN_RIDGE.

title: Harmless: mirrored bend twins differ only in vertex count (202/203 ridge, 204/207 slab), all vertices on the ideal arc within 1 nm
evidence: rv.cell_shapes: route_l1_1 bend 2 ridge has 202 vertices and its slab 207, the mirror twin in route_l1_0 has 203/204 (bend 1 of l1_1 slab 202). Distance of every vertex to the ideal R=79.5/80.5 (ridge) and 75/85 um (slab) circle about the bend centre (work/twins/s10.py): max 0.6-0.7 nm for all 8 bend polygons. Whole-chip mirror XOR about y=0 (work/twins/s6.py): apart from the posted defects, only slivers of 0.0001-0.005 um2 along the arcs (e.g. here, [633.0,+-25], [1215-1296,+-137..+-371], [1795-1884,+-385..+-441]). Normalised s-bend twins (5 output s-bends, 4 level-2 s-bends): Hausdorff <= 6 nm.
impact: None: nm-level arc discretisation, far below the litho grid effect; no loss, no length change (< 0.001 um).
